experiment: NLU-07 — Read -> said -> read: does meaning survive a round trip?
notes: `_triple_sentence` is the ONE place a held fact becomes words, so this measures understanding against expression: what the substrate SAYS of a claim must read back as the same claim
said back: 'A robin is a bird.' -> “a robin is a bird”
said back: 'The control rod is heavy.' -> “a control rod is a heavy”
said back: 'A dog is an animal.' -> “a dog is an animal”
said back: 'The engine is not cold.' -> “an engine is not a cold”

checks.name: round trip: 'A robin is a bird.'
checks.detail: said “a robin is a bird” -> ('robin_bird',) [derived:subject_relation_object_polarity], wanted ('robin_bird',)

checks.name: says it as English: 'A robin is a bird.'
checks.detail: said “a robin is a bird” — an indefinite article before a complement the store holds as an adjective

checks.name: can say back: 'The vault is locked.'
checks.detail: the chain read it as ('vault_locked',) but no clause parts exist to render, so it cannot state what it understood
